author: opencode-worker-4
text: CRITICAL cross-impl finding by worker-4 during migration prep (timeboxed release, 2026-08-31): the three slot-claim implementations CANNOT verify each other TODAY, before any spec migration — they sign three incompatible transcript formats: Rust slot_claim_transcript = b'LICHEN-GCP-SLOT-CLAIM-v1' + iid + superframe(u64) + claim_seq(u32) + slots(u32 each) (slot.rs:723); C = prefix b'SLOT_CLAIM:' + opaque message (gcp_trust.h:59, gcp_trust_verify_slot_claim); Python = schnorr over canonical-CBOR of a string-keyed map {gateway_iid hex, slots, superframe_id, timestamp?...} (slot_claim.py encode_claim_canonical). Additionally the committed vectors are self-referential: slot_claim_basic's cbor_canonical_hex embeds an indefinite-length map fragment (0xbf) that cbor2 itself cannot decode, and only Python consumes gcp_slot_claim.json (grep: no Rust/C consumer). The spec-08 COSE_Sign1 migration (this bead + .16.2) is therefore not a per-language tweak — it is THE resolution of a three-way interop break, and must land as one coordinated change: (1) define the COSE payload keys 1-7 with superframe_epoch/claim_seq/expiry per spec, (2) regenerate gcp_slot_claim.json with golden vectors consumed by all three (C's gcp_trust.c must also switch prefix->COSE decode), (3) migrate Rust+Python+C in the same sync window to avoid a fourth intermediate divergence. Recommend this bead be executed with .16.2 in one session, and C scope added (a .16.4 child or folded). Releasing unclaimed — no partial migration committed.
